segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [soft wind rustling tent fabric] [softly] Keep your eyes open or softly lowered. Imagine checking the coordinates of a calm campsite after dark.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find five things you can see. Colour, edge, shadow, texture, light. Let each become a marker around the tent.
[soft, slow, warm voice] One... two... three... four... five... You are here, in this particular place.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft fabric rustling] Notice four things you can feel: feet, clothing, seat, air, hands, or warmth.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let contact points become tent pegs holding attention close to the ground.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find three sounds. Perhaps one is distant, one is near, and one belongs to your body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice two scents or two qualities of the air. Faint and neutral both count.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice one taste. Let the smallest ordinary sensation complete the campsite map.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Thoughts can remain beyond the firelight. They are not the only coordinates available.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest with the strongest physical contact point for several breaths.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Look around and name where you are, the approximate time, and one gentle next action.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Pack only what you need. Leave the campsite slowly and return to the ordinary room.
